summary.title: How To Own Your Growth As A Software Engineer
summary.one_liner: You learn a mental model (the Rigor/Relevance Framework) for matching your work to each engineering level, plus ways to advocate for yourself and communicate well.
takeaways: Expectations change by level: juniors mostly learn, mid-level engineers build, seniors design, and leads collaborate.
The Rigor/Relevance Framework maps acquisition, application, assimilation and adaptation onto junior, mid-level, senior and staff+ roles.
Treat leveling guides as imperfect maps; don't chase boxes or titles, since titles lag behind impact.
Advocate for yourself by journaling milestones, tracking time, and sharing achievements broadly.
Build writing and communication skills early, starting with a few external posts or internal memos per year.
summary.summary: The author, Jesal Gadhia, describes how an engineer's focus shifts from learning to building, designing and collaborating as they move up levels. He uses the Rigor/Relevance Framework from the International Center for Leadership in Education to describe expectations for junior, mid-level, senior and staff+ engineers, and notes that leveling guides are imperfect maps. The post then covers advocating for yourself through reflection, tracking work and sharing achievements, and building writing skills with personal knowledge management tools. It links to outside resources on career growth and writing throughout.
